name: Gagne
role: Sergeant in charge of weapons, in Larry's telling; a French Foreign Legionnaire, he says
summary: Named by Larry for the first time on 2026-09-01, pronounced Gone-yay. Describing the night the Special Forces camp at Đồng Xoài was attacked, he said: "Gagne was with me and died, he was a french foreign Legionair." Asked again a day later where Gagne was when he died, Larry answered: "No - he did not die. He was still alive when I got medivac out." And later still: "I have no idea. He could still be alive for all I know." All three answers are his, and all are kept. Gagne is the man who got Larry his Thompson: "Gagne got me this. He went into the special forces armory, signed it out and handed it to me. He was in charge of the armory" (VN-0082); and on 2026-09-12, "It was mine and I got it from Gagne. He was in charge of all the weapons at Ton Son Nhut" (VN-0013). "Sargent Gagne made Field Promotion to Lieutenant and that don't really happen. He was that good." Larry places him at his own first arrival on the mountain: "When I first got there (Nui Ba Den for the first time) with Gagne."
researchNotes: The name and its spelling are Larry's own, given on the telephone and checked with him more than once; on 2026-09-02 his son also recorded the pronunciation as "Gone-yay". The fate is contradicted by Larry himself and is not reconciled here: on 2026-09-01 he said Gagne died; on 2026-09-02, asked directly, he said Gagne did not die (data/recollections/giscus-stories-c18259589.json); on 2026-09-03, "He could still be alive for all I know." Nothing is corrected in any record. The consequence for research: a man who survived Larry's tour would not appear in DCAS or on the Virtual Wall at all, so casualty files are the wrong records to search. Nationality: asked whether Gagne was French himself he said "Yes, pretty sure," then widened it, "He could have been born in Germany or Belgium, I don't know." That is consistent with the Legion, which recruits foreigners by design and has historically enlisted men under assumed identities, so a French record set is a reasonable first place to look but not a safe assumption. 2026-09-05 (giscus-stories-c18308877, giscus-vn-0041-c18308745): a battlefield commission from sergeant to lieutenant is exactly the kind of thing that leaves paper (direct appointments were published in orders), so Gagne as a sergeant and as a lieutenant doubles the ways a roster can find him. A French Foreign Legionnaire could not have held a U.S. commission; either the Legion is his past, or one of the two descriptions is not literally so. Recorded, not reconciled. Where he ran the weapons is also split: the Special Forces armory in the 2026-09-02 account, and "all the weapons at Ton Son Nhut" at VN-0013 on 2026-09-12, while his other appearances put him on the mountain. Recorded as given. The 2026-09-02 comment also carries a remark by Larry about Gagne and Lowry; it was moved out of this record on 2026-09-14 to research/people/sgt-lowry-search.md, and that recollection is not linked to this person, so it does not render on his page. Linking it is a family decision.
